ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A current-carrying straight wire is placed parallel to the x-axis, the direction of the uniform magnetic field is parallel to the xOy coordinate plane, and the Ampere force on the wire is F. If this wire is made into a $\frac{3}{4}$ circular ring and placed in the xOy coordinate plane (as shown in the figure), the current is kept unchanged, and the line connecting the two endpoints a and b is parallel to the x-axis, then what is the magnitude of the Ampere force on this circular ring?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the x-axis of the coordinate system is horizontal to the right, the y-axis is vertical upward, and the center of the circle is marked as O. The wire is bent into a circular arc located in the xOy plane; the arc occupies the upper part and most of the two sides of the whole circle, with a segment missing at the bottom. The two endpoints are marked a and b respectively, located at the lower left and lower right of the circle, and a and b are at the same horizontal height, so the line ab is parallel to the x-axis. From the figure it can be seen that this is a 3/4 circular ring missing the lower 1/4 circular arc. Reasoning: Suppose the length of the straight wire before being bent into the circular ring is equal to the arc length, and the radius of the circle is R, then the wire length is L=\frac{3}{4}\cdot 2\pi R=\frac{3\pi R}{2}. The original straight wire is parallel to the x-axis; suppose the direction of the uniform magnetic field makes an angle θ with the x-axis, then the magnitude of the Ampere force originally received is F=IBL\sinθ=IB\frac{3\pi R}{2}\sinθ. In a uniform magnetic field, the resultant Ampere force on a current-carrying wire of any shape is I\int d\vec l\times \vec B. Since \vec B is constant, it can be equivalent to the Ampere force on the straight wire connecting the two endpoints of the wire, namely I(\vec r_b-\vec r_a)\times \vec B. In the figure, what the circular arc lacks is 1/4 of a circle, corresponding to the shorter chord between endpoints a and b, and the central angle is 90°, therefore |ab|=2R\sin45°=\sqrt2R. Also, ab is parallel to the x-axis, so its angle with the magnetic field is still θ. The magnitude of the resultant Ampere force on the circular ring is F'=IB|ab|\sinθ=IB\sqrt2R\sinθ. Dividing the two equations: \frac{F'}{F}=\frac{IB\sqrt2R\sinθ}{IB(3\pi R/2)\sinθ}=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3\pi}. Therefore the magnitude of the Ampere force on the circular ring is \frac{2\sqrt2}{3\pi}F.
